findings.description: Cloud design stages cannot execute unattended in CI due to interactive personal subscription requirements, necessitating a split workflow where developers run cloud stages locally and transfer state to CI.
findings.subject: subscription_conflict_statement

findings.description: Exporting run state containing confidential source trees and protected tests to CI artifact storage (Jenkins stashes or GitLab job artifacts) introduces risk of confidential data leakage if the adopter uses shared or cloud-backed CI runners.
findings.subject: ci_adapter_jenkins_gitlab

findings.description: Connecting guest VM or WSL2 sandboxes to host-managed local models (Ollama, llama-server) over a virtual network bridge complicates egress verification compared to single-kernel Linux bwrap loopback setups.
findings.subject: os_portability_matrix

findings.description: Refusing model dispatching stages natively on Windows and macOS preserves isolation guarantees but requires developers on those platforms to manage external virtualization prerequisites (WSL2, Lima, UTM) outside the uv distribution.
findings.subject: isolation_backend_layer

findings.description: Adopting repositories must keep .agentic/pipeline.lock synchronized with agentic-pipeline package versions during upgrades to prevent runtime failures from lock-hash drift.
findings.subject: adoption_model

cost.evidence: The design uses existing personal subscriptions and local models without adding API keys, paid endpoints, or paid third-party dependencies.

maintainability.evidence: The package depends exclusively on the Python standard library with no new third-party dependencies, preserving run formats and pinning defaults via .agentic/pipeline.lock.

reliability.evidence: CI job chaining enforces integrity through sha256 manifests, sealed input verification, and frozen digest checks at each state import.

scalability.evidence: Inability to run cloud stages unattended in CI forces a hybrid local-to-CI handoff, restricting automated throughput and scaling.

security.evidence: Bwrap isolation is preserved across platforms by refusing model stages on native Windows/macOS, vendor OAuth tokens are isolated in tmpfs sandboxes, and offline human signatures are bound to the log tip.
